name: Stewed Ox-Tails
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Divide the tails at the joints, wash, and put them into a stew-pan with sufficient water to cover, and set them on the fire.
When the water boils remove the scum, and add the onions cut into rings, the spice, seasoning and herbs.
Cover the stew-pan closely, and simmer gently until tender, which will be in about two and one-half hours.
Take the tails out, make a thickening of butter and flour; add it to the gravy, and let it boil for one-quarter of an hour.
Strain it through a sieve into a saucepan; put back the tails, add the lemon juice and catsup; let the whole just boil up, and serve.
Serve with croutons or sippets of toasted bread.

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Divide the tails at the joints, wash, and put them into a stew-pan with sufficient water to cover, and set them on the fire.
2. When the water boils remove the scum, and add the onions cut into rings, the spice, seasoning and herbs.
3. Cover the stew-pan closely, and simmer gently until tender, which will be in about two and one-half hours.
4. Take the tails out, make a thickening of butter and flour; add it to the gravy, and let it boil for one-quarter of an hour.
5. Strain it through a sieve into a saucepan; put back the tails, add the lemon juice and catsup; let the whole just boil up, and serve.
6. Serve with croutons or sippets of toasted bread.
